pairs.question: Nam qua alia re praestare ceteris poterimus, si ea, quae ex te accepimus, omnium prosus fient communia? quippe ego doctrina anteire malim quam copiis atque opulentiis.
pairs.answer: Acroaticos libros, quos editos quereris et non proinde ut arcana absconditos, neque editos scito esse neque non editos, quoniam his solis cognobiles erunt, qui nos audiverunt.
pairs.derivation: Alexander's letter (section VIII) to Aristotle, complaining the esoteric books were published; the speech tag 'inquit' (interpolated mid-quote, 'Nam qua inquit alia re') is dropped as framing and the contiguous utterance is kept, first letter capitalized. It contains a genuine interrogative ('qua alia re praestare ceteris poterimus...?'). Aristotle's reply (section IX) is taken with its framing 'Rescripsit ei Aristoteles ad hanc sententiam:' dropped; the entire quoted reply answers the worry by asserting the books are effectively neither published nor unpublished, intelligible only to his hearers. Chapter VI (Apollinaris), VIII (Annianus), X (grammarian) and I.IX were dropped: their questions are narrated indirect discourse rather than quoted interrogatives, or the replies are refusals/deflections rather than answers.
